about: The owner, 2026-10-11, on the Ask answer for "What have I saved about courses & study?": "I want it more dynamic and better at language ... seeing the context for uni, classes, next week (in comparison to the current datetime and the datetime that note was written), this semester, and the class names". A rule as well as a gold: a note's relative time is resolved against the day it was written and said again from today, and a note's connected facts are told in flowing sentences with a reporting verb, not label lines; citations kept. The same note on two days: the week it was written (the owner's own wording is the gold) and months later.

paragraphs_about: The owner, 2026-10-11, on the same answer: "it didnt do the understanding and rewrite for the rest of the response, only the first paragraph and note". Every note with a heading of its own (a lecture, a lab, a plan) is a paragraph of prose that understands it, its verbs varied; a relative time is named as a day ("before next week" written 22 July is before 27 July; "a week later" says its day); the open plan is said once, in its own paragraph. The day a note was written is said only when the question asks about time (INBOX 1441, the owner, 2026-10-29: "I dont like how it refers to dates"), so a paragraph no longer opens on it.
